decision: Confirmed; retain High severity with explicit scope
evidence: GenericWorker.run emits error when save throws, then finished unconditionally (app/thread_worker.py:33-37). TaskRunnerController wires both callbacks, without filtering finished after an error (app/controllers/task_runner.py:69-77, 109-117).

autosave_project.on_finished unconditionally deletes recovery on a regular-project target and marks clean when dirty revision has not changed (app/controllers/projects.py:417-424); on_error does not set a failure guard (409-415).

Production has_unsaved_changes/set_project_clean logic confirms marking clean clears manual dirty and all undo clean flags (controller.py:373-395). Close prompts only when has_unsaved_changes is true (controller.py:848-878).

Independent execution used actual GenericWorker, TaskRunnerController, autosave_project, clear_recovery_checkpoint, has_unsaved_changes, and set_project_clean methods with Qt Signal/QTimer shims and a real temporary recovery file. Injected OSError(28, No space left on device). Observed no clean-state simulation stub: production dirty methods were used.
counterarguments_and_scope: Not every autosave failure loses clean state: the regular-project path requires project_autosave_enabled and a project_file; recovery-only interval saves do not run the destructive clean branch.
When dirty revision changes during the failed save, the project remains dirty and a retry is scheduled. Recovery is still deleted on that path.
Per-page batch autosave repeats the same unconditional finished clean logic; independent runtime reproduction focused regular autosave, with batch confirmed by source.
A pre-existing recovery file must exist for deletion to remove actual recovery data; otherwise deletion is a no-op but false-clean/close suppression still applies.
The SQLite writer may preserve the last successfully saved project via transactional behavior; report loss of latest unsaved edits, not unavoidable corruption of the entire prior project.

No live Qt event loop or real disk-full GUI run. Signal/timer shims were used. The core failure does not rely on callback ordering beyond finished eventually running, since its destructive branch contains no success guard.
